scope.requirements:
# Clean design specification
Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.

This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.

findings.title: Sponsor prize release can transfer into a subsequently registered raffle clone
findings.description:
Source-supported candidate, low severity and needs human review. Sponsor-recipient screening is performed at creation/initialization against the current same-factory registry. A sponsorRecipient equal to a future clone address is then code-less and unregistered, so it can pass. If that address subsequently becomes another raffle clone before the first raffle returns its NFT, releaseSponsorPrize uses transferFrom to the stored recipient without repeating _isProtocolDestination. A standard ERC721 transfer bypasses the receiving clone receiver hook and ownerOf then confirms the new clone, so the first raffle marks the prize claimed even though the second clone only has release paths for its own configured prize. This violates the stated no movement between raffle clones property and can strand the returned NFT. The quote-token release path does repeat the destination check, making this omission specific to the sponsor NFT return. Impact requires the sponsor-selected future-address recipient; no arbitrary theft from normally configured raffles is established. Defensive property: prize return must reject a recipient that is registered protocol plumbing at delivery time. An execution check remains outstanding.
Assumptions: The sponsor selects an as-yet undeployed future same-factory clone address as sponsorRecipient, distinct from the clone being initialized.; That address is deployed and registered before a CashWon or Refunding sponsor-prize return.; The prize is an ordinary standards-compliant ERC721 and differs from the receiving clone's configured prize.; This is a recipient-selection edge case, not demonstrated theft from an honest sponsor who selected an address they control.

Docker daemon access was unavailable in the supplementary environment check; no locally usable pinned tool image was established. No test-inclusive plan is permitted without that prerequisite. No tests were supplied in the authorized target.

Clean DESIGN calls arbitrary prize contracts untrusted; IRaffle.sol:13-15 assumes honest standards-compliant prizes. Interface support, callback parameters and ownerOf assertions cannot establish honest escrow/delivery or future transferability of an arbitrary hostile prize. This is a trust-boundary/design limitation, not a separately demonstrated canonical-token exploit.

Canonical USDC and Chainlink wrapper implementations/deployment parameters are not supplied. The consumer base and interfaces are reviewed; canonical identity, deployed max gas/confirmations, billing and callback delivery are unverified.

All 31 selected dependency source files are included and hash-verified. Primary dependency call paths were inspected; unused/transitive library routines were not comprehensively audited. Lockfile relevant package entries were inspected, not all monorepo packages.

Counterfactual and foreign-factory recipients, arbitrary contract recipients unable to operate a ticket or NFT, token pause/blacklist restrictions and unsolicited assets can limit exits. Beyond the documented future-clone prize-return candidate, no additional actionable source-supported fault is claimed.
The supplied target SHA is recorded as operator provenance. No target git history or external repository was consulted to independently authenticate that SHA.
